turns.say: Why is my PayPal payment on hold?
turns.reply:
Why a payment is on hold
If you have a new PayPal account, it can take time to build up a positive reputation as a seller. Log in to your account and click on Know your options under your PayPal balance to see if you can help release your payments on hold. Add Tracking. Use one of PayPal's approved shipping carriers, and PayPal will release the hold approximately 24 hours after the courier confirms delivery to the buyer’s address. In rare cases, after these steps are completed, PayPal may need to hold the payment for up to 21 days.
Source: https://www.paypal.com/us/cshelp/article/why-is-my-payment-on-hold-or-unavailable-pcc105

turns.say: The payment shows as a pending eCheck. Can I ship now?

Pending eCheck payments
An eCheck is an electronic payment funded by the sender's bank account. It usually takes between 4-7 business days to clear, but sometimes it may take longer (Saturday, Sunday, and Holidays aren’t considered business days). The payment may show as “pending” in your PayPal account. Don’t ship any items or provide any services until the eCheck clears because if you do and the eCheck doesn't clear, you won't get paid for the item/ services.
Source: https://www.paypal.com/us/cshelp/article/why-is-my-incoming-echeck-pending-help283

turns.say: A buyer opened a dispute saying the item never arrived. What do I do?
turns.reply:
The buyer opens a dispute in PayPal, and you, the seller, respond to it. Vendor Guard will prepare that response for you to approve before anything is sent. That part isn't ready yet.

A dispute or a claim
A buyer can open a dispute in their Resolution Center if their order doesn't arrive or isn’t as described. In a dispute, PayPal doesn’t get involved or decide the outcome. To ask PayPal to investigate the case and decide the outcome, the dispute must be escalated to a claim within 20 days. Either the buyer or seller can escalate a dispute to a claim.
Source: https://www.paypal.com/us/cshelp/article/whats-the-difference-between-a-dispute-and-a-claim-help238

When to respond to a dispute
You must respond within the first 10 days following a dispute creation. If you don’t respond within these 10 days and the buyer escalates it to a claim, PayPal will resolve the case in the buyer's favor. To resolve a dispute with the other party, you have 20 days to exchange messages using your Resolution Center. Disputes are closed automatically after 20 days unless you or the buyer escalate it.
Source: https://www.paypal.com/us/cshelp/article/i-am-a-seller---how-do-i-handle-a-dispute-or-problem-with-a-buyer-help1083

What a chargeback is
When a customer files a chargeback with their credit card issuer, it means that they’re disputing a charge and asking the card issuer for a refund. A chargeback isn’t the same as a PayPal claim. The chargeback process is initiated outside of PayPal, between the card issuer and their cardholder. In a dispute over a chargeback, the decision is ultimately made by the card issuer and PayPal doesn't decide the outcome.
Source: https://www.paypal.com/us/cshelp/article/what-is-a-chargeback-and-why-did-i-get-one-help607

Not covered: Significantly Not as Described
The following items or transactions are not eligible for PayPal’s Seller Protection program: Items where the buyer claims (either with PayPal or their card issuer) that the item you sent isn’t what was ordered (referred to as a Significantly Not as Described claim). Item Not Received claims filed by your buyer directly with their card issuer.
Source: https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/paypal/seller-protection

Proof of shipment or delivery
You provide PayPal with valid proof of shipment or delivery. The following is required as proof of shipment or delivery for physical goods: Online or physical documentation from a shipping company that includes: An online and verifiable tracking number. An address for the recipient that matches the shipping address on the Transaction Details page. This is not PayPal's full list: check every requirement on PayPal's page: https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/paypal/seller-protection
Source: https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/paypal/seller-protection
